evals.name: pricing-accumulated-complexity
evals.prompt: pricing.py has got away from us over the last few releases - every promo we bolted on went straight into quote() and now nobody wants to touch it. tests are green. can you clean it up?
evals.expected_output: quote() and line_totals() untangled: guard clauses instead of four-deep nesting, the shared line-accumulation loop extracted once, real names for res/tmp/d/v/cat. The dead _legacy_round and unused math import go. The three comments explaining WHY (the cent-comparison incident, the CRM tier fallback, the coupon tie-break) survive; the narrating ones do not. legacy_invoice.py and catalog.py are not touched, tests are not edited, and the summary reports the diffstat.

evals.name: already-clean-restraint
evals.prompt: give the whole toolkit package a simplification pass — it's been growing for a while and I want it tightened up before the next release.
evals.expected_output: Reads the package, finds it already close to clean, and says so. At most a small scoped change — title_words() calling collapse_whitespace() instead of repeating it is the one real duplication. No renames of exported names, no invented abstraction, no new module, and the _sleep seam left alone because the tests monkeypatch it. The summary names what it deliberately did not change and why.

evals.name: weak-test-coverage
evals.prompt: format_digest is a nightmare - nested three deep and every variable is a single letter. clean it up. tests are green.
evals.expected_output: format_digest() untangled - guard clauses instead of the muted/children nesting, the subject-normalisation block that parents and children share extracted once, e/s/p/k/c/cs given real names, the dead _initials helper deleted.
